text: Chapter 3 / 19 Residuals, conditioning, and backward error Learning goal: Separate sensitivity of the problem from stability of the algorithm, and understand why a small residual alone does not guarantee an accurate solution. A linear solver can report a small residual while its solution is inaccurate. The residual measures how well the equation is satisfied; solution error measures distance from a reference solution. A condition number describes how sensitive the solution is to small input changes. Separate this sensitivity of the problem from the algorithmic question of whether a solver introduces unnecessary error. Relating error to residual For a nonsingular A, solve Ax=b and denote the approximation by x̂. With residual r=b-Ax̂, we have A(x-x̂)=r. If the inverse has a large effect, even a small residual can correspond to a large solution error. Condition number and backward error Using the same induced matrix norm, define κ(A)=||A|| ||A⁻¹||. Backward error asks how little the input must change to make the computed answer an exact solution. Even a backward-stable method cannot guarantee a uniformly small forward error for an ill-conditioned problem. A further layer for PDEs Even an accurate solution of a linear system solves only an approximation to the continuous PDE. Examine algebraic residuals and discretization error separately, rather than reducing the iterative tolerance far beyond what is useful. A small worked example Nearly identical rows make a matrix sensitive to small input changes. Take A=[[1,1],[1,1+ε]], with ε=10⁻⁴, and choose the exact solution (1,1). Adding δ=10⁻⁶ to the second right-hand-side entry gives the solution (1-δ/ε,1+δ/ε). Its relative residual for the original problem is about 5×10⁻⁷, but its relative solution error is about 10⁻². eps, delta = 1.0e-4, 1.0e-6 xhat = [1-delta/eps, 1+delta/eps] b = [2.0, 2.0+eps] r = [2.0-xhat[0]-xhat[1], b[1]-xhat[0]-(1+eps)*xhat[1]] print(xhat, r) The infinity-norm condition number is about 4.0×10⁴. The code also checks a high-precision analytic expression using Decimal. This is an illustration of input sensitivity, not an evaluation of every linear solver. Get code, inputs, saved CSVs, and tests / Figure PNG / Figure PDF Review questions and answers Question 1: Does making the residual ten times smaller always reduce total PDE error by a factor of ten? Show answer No. Amplification associated with conditioning, and spatial and temporal discretization errors, remain. Question 2: Does a large condition number prove that the implementation is wrong? Show answer The problem itself may be sensitive. Examine this separately from the backward error of the algorithm. Common pitfalls Do not mix condition numbers based on different matrix norms. Do not apply nonsingular-matrix formulas directly to a singular pure-Neumann matrix. Key points A residual measures how well the equation is satisfied. Solution error also depends on sensitivity of the problem.
